subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must transform an equation while preserving the same solution set
use when a later algebra step fails after a valid model or equation has already been formed
anchor: An equation is a claim that two expressions have the same value; a legal transformation preserves that claim for every solution.
ordinary_language_bridge: Whatever change is made to one side must preserve the same equality relation on the other side; moving a term is shorthand for a legal inverse operation, not deletion.
reconstruction_route: substitute the candidate back into the original relation

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: same equation, same target variable, same starting line
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: subtract the same term from both sides versus deleting a term from one side
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which next line remains equivalent to the original equation, and why?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: the operation must preserve the solution set

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: terms can be moved or cancelled without an equivalent operation
misconception_discriminator.probe: present two visually similar next steps, one legal and one unilateral; require justification
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner identifies the operation applied to both sides and rejects unilateral deletion

repair_route: return to equality meaning before symbol movement
contrast legal inverse operation with unilateral deletion
retry on a new equation without preselected operation
verification_method: substitute the final value into the original equation
for a system, replay both original equations
known_limitations: does not by itself teach sign arithmetic
does not establish a preferred system-solving method for every structure
